conviction_note: Near-coin-flip with a slight negative lean: the company's own numbers (H1 $69.3m, Q3 guided flat to slightly above Q2's $32.9m) leave the FY $142-148m guide needing an above-seasonal Q4 of roughly $38-45m, so a second cut or a narrowing to the low end is a real risk on a name that has fallen on 7 of its last 8 prints. Offsetting that, about 10% of shares are short (8-11 days to cover) and the market cap (~$135m) sits close to cash (~$97m at Q2), so a print that only holds the guide could squeeze. abs_move 14 comes from the 15.1% median reaction, trimmed slightly because no first guide is due. p_up 45. The per-finding sum (-1.2) and the scaled number (-1.4) agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: From the company's own numbers, the FY2026 guide needs a Q4 ramp well above seasonal. H1 revenue is $69.3m (Q1 $36.4m + Q2 $32.9m) and the FY guide is $142-148m, so H2 must be $72.7-78.7m. With Q3 guided flat to slightly above Q2 (about $33-34.5m), Q4 has to be about $38.2-45.7m, which is +11% to +38% sequential. Q4/Q3 was +9% in 2025 ($40.2m to $43.9m) and -2% in 2024 ($35.8m to $35.2m). On that seasonality, a Q3 of about $34m gives a Q4 of $35-37m and a FY of about $139-142m, at or below the low end. So the release (bmo 2026-11-09) carries a material chance of a second cut or a narrowing to the low end. The market's bar is the unchanged $142-148m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guide cut (2026-08-10, FY $169-174m to $142-148m plus breakeven pushed to 2027) brought -39.95%. 2026-05-06 (Q2 then missed its own guide by about 9%): -16.41%. The 2026-01-08 +23.81% preceded a Q4 2025 beat ($43.9m vs about $38m). The guide line has moved this stock more than anything else.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews show only a single-quarter revenue consensus ($34.5-37.0m) and the unchanged FY range. If the market were pricing a cut, the Q3 consensus would sit at or below the company's flat-to-Q2 range, not at its top ($34.53m) or above it ($37.0m). The -12.6% 20-day drift may price part of it.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 revenue come from separate releases: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/quanterix-releases-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-of-2025 (Q3 2025 $40.2m, Q3 2024 $35.8m) and https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/quanterix-releases-financial-results-for-the-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025 (Q4 2025 $43.9m, Q4 2024 $35.2m). The 10-Q says instrument softness is expected to continue for the rest of 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001503274/000150327426000036/qtrx-20260630.htm). Counterweight: a new CFO set this guide in August explicitly assuming no end-market improvement, which suggests some cushion, and Q4 is the budget-flush quarter.

findings.finding: The consensus revenue bar for Q3 ($34.53m from 6 analysts on FXEmpire; $37.0m on Benzinga) sits at or above the top of the company's own guide of flat to slightly above Q2's $32.9m. A print in the middle of the guide (about $33.5m) would therefore read as a small miss against the street, after Q2 missed by 12-14% ($32.91m vs $37.5-38.2m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by about 13%: -39.95% (together with the guide cut). Q4 2025 beat by about 15%: +23.81%. Q1 2026 headline in line, organic -21%: -16.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street numbers appear not to have been brought down to the company's flat-to-Q2 commentary. If they had, consensus would read about $33-34m, and the two sources would not disagree by $2.5m.
findings.independence: Benzinga's $37.0m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/QTRX/earnings-forecasts) points the same way, but the two sources disagree with each other, so the bar is disputed and this finding is capped small. It shares the Q3-guide document with finding 1, but this one is about the quarter and finding 1 is about the FY guide.

findings.finding: Peer prints since Quanterix last spoke point to stable consumables and weak instruments in life-science tools. 10x Genomics Q3 2026 (2026-11-05): revenue +1%, consumables +5%, US +6%, FY guide raised to $625-635m, but instruments -43% and spatial instruments $3.1m vs $7.1m. Bruker Q3 2026 (2026-11-04): +0.7% organic, FY targets kept. For Quanterix that supports recurring Simoa and Akoya consumables and services, and is negative for spatial (PhenoCycler) and Simoa instrument placements.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history for peer read-throughs. Quanterix's own instrument weakness was blamed for the Q1 and Q2 shortfalls (-16% and -40%).
findings.why_not_priced: Both prints are 1-2 sessions old and QTRX has not moved on them (5-day -1.4%). It is a proxy, and the market may reasonably ignore it for a company with company-specific execution problems.
findings.independence: Bruker Q3 2026 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001109354/000119312526446176/brkr-ex99_1.htm (flat organic, targets kept). This is a proxy: Quanterix itself blamed company-specific commercial execution as well as the market.

findings.finding: Short positioning is moderately crowded into the print: 4.68m shares short (about 9.9% of shares outstanding), 8.4 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement (about 11 on the baseline's ADV). At $2.865 the market cap is about $135m against $96.9m of cash and securities at Q2 (guided to about $80m at year end, no debt). A print that holds the FY guide and shows Q3 cash use near Q2's $4.0m gives shorts little room and supplies a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only up print in 8 (+23.81% on 2026-01-08) came on a beat from a depressed price, which is consistent with a squeeze response when the news is merely not bad.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is falling slightly (5.05m to 4.68m), not building, so shorts are not pressing into the print. Near-cash valuations are common in tools microcaps and the squeeze only fires conditionally, so this is a skewed payoff rather than an expected drift.
findings.independence: Cash figure from the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001503274/000150327426000035/ex991-qtrxx20260630.htm). Shares outstanding 47.29m per the same equibles page. This is the one place the squeeze concern is counted; finding 1 was not shrunk for it again.

findings.finding: Q2 adjusted cash usage was only $4.0m, down from $14.8m in Q1 ($18.8m for H1). But the guide from $96.9m to about $80m at year end implies about $17m of H2 use, roughly $8.5m a quarter. If Q3 use repeats Q2's run-rate, cash could come in above the implied path, which matters for a stock valued near cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash guidance moved with the -39.95% August reaction (YE $100m to $80m, breakeven to 2027). There is no isolated history on the cash line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference: the gap between the Q2 run-rate and the implied H2 burn may be planned (a debt payoff to reach 'no debt', severance), so it could be fully explained by known uses.
findings.independence: None outside the same 8-K. It shares that document with finding 1.

baseline_tension: Without a skew there is no directional option statement. The -12.6% 20-day drift and 1-of-8 up history agree with the negative guide-risk finding, which suggests part of it is priced. The crowded short and near-cash valuation cut against it, so p_up is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: $34.53m vs $37.0m): finding 2, which depends on consensus, stays capped at -1.0 with its range narrowed. Finding 1 rests on the company guide, not consensus, so it is unchanged.
Rule 7 (crowded short): the squeeze is counted once, as its own +1.5 positioning finding, and finding 1 is not shrunk a second time.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': p_up moved from 44 to 45, so expected_move goes from -1.68 to -1.40. No finding sizes changed, so impact_sum is -1.2 both pre and post.
